thread:
Maria L.: quick Q — for /v2/generate with structured responses, are we going to require clients to send Content-Type/Accept headers? saw some SDKs omit them and the proxy currently defaults to application/json, but that feels brittle. :thinking:
Sam P.: we intentionally default to application/json to avoid breaking existing clients. i don't want to return 406 unless absolutely necessary. we should instead be explicit in docs and add a helpful warning header during transition (e.g., X-Redwood-Contract-Warning).
Jen K.: agree on non-breaking default. action: add a schema validation warning when request lacks Accept/Content-Type and body looks like JSON — not blocking, just emit a metric and header. will open PR for lint + tests.
Oliver R.: quick note on nullable fields: do we want schema validator to treat null vs missing differently? earlier canary showed SDKs treating missing as older clients. i'd prefer validators accept both for optional fields but fail if field present and wrong type.
Maria L.: yes — optional fields should be permissive (null | missing). required fields must be present and non-null. this matches client behavior we saw. put that in the RFC doc.
Sam P.: implementation detail: runtime will be doing a JSON schema check post-model-output. suggest we add a small schema field `allowNullForOptional=true` to the contract so teams can override for strict endpoints.
Jen K.: that override makes sense. default permissive, opt-in strict. i'll add it to the API contract proto.
Maria L.: another edge: streaming ndjson path — when we stream structured chunks, some clients parse line-by-line and choke on `null` as a field value. we should document streaming examples.
Oliver R.: streaming: add example in SDKs with a robust parser that tolerates `\n` separators and missing keys. also include a `Content-Type: application/x-ndjson` example in docs.
Jen K.: draft curl examples coming — sample request and response (non-streaming + streaming). quick snippet for non-blocking validation check:
```
# non-blocking check: warn header if missing
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v2/generate
# response may include: X-Redwood-Contract-Warning: missing-accept-header
```
Sam P.: +1. also add a canary that flips `allowNullForOptional`=false to test strict clients. we can run internal SDKs against it.
deploy-bot: canary deployed to infra/canary-01 (build 2026.3.11) :rocket:
Maria L.: can someone from eng-runtime confirm fallback behavior if model returns a top-level null for an expected object? do we coerce to {} or reject?
Oliver R.: eng-runtime prefers rejecting (emit structured error) because coercions hide regressions. but for customer-facing public endpoints we might coerce to `{}` and emit warning. need policy.
Jen K.: proposal: internal endpoints (platform tools) = strict reject; public endpoints = coerce+warn by default, opt-in strict. i'll codify.
Sam P.: sounds good. tagging @eng-runtime for final sign-off and then i'll add a small note in the rollforward checklist.
Maria L.: thanks. Jen — assign the PR to me and sam for review. i'll update the RFC and add a dot-point for SDK teams to add Accept header. :thumbsup:
